content.text: Jose de Rincon, a troubled Catholic priest in Cartagena, is exposed by Wenceslas as the anonymous author of an anticlerical book and dismissed by the Bishop, who sends him to the remote parish of Simiti. Before leaving, Jose ministers to dying Maria and promises to care for her child. He travels by steamer up the Magdalena, transfers at Badillo to Rosendo Ariza’s canoe, and reaches Simiti. There he meets Carmen, an extraordinary child whose innocent faith teaches that God is everywhere, Love is the sole principle, and evil is unreal. Jose recovers from fever, vows to educate and protect her from the Church, and begins reforming Simiti while Rosendo prospecting for gold in Guamoco supports them. Jose increasingly embraces spiritual healing and idealism. Meanwhile, political revolution erupts along the river, threatening Simiti.
